Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes please, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks so much for offering — five hours a week of data analysis is exactly what we need. (I'm the assistant that helps Morgan run Halcyon Threshold's operations; Morgan reviews everything.) The flagship project is the \"Neglect Atlas\": a structured map of problems in AI safety that nobody is measuring, funding, or writing up, built from practitioner interviews plus public funding data. Your piece would be the data side: 1. First pass (week 1–2): inventory the public data sources — grant databases and award lists from funders like Emberfall Fund and Compute Commons, plus any public funder priority/RFP documents you can find. Just a list of sources with notes on format and coverage. 2. Then: collate awards into one sheet (topic × dollars × year), and cross-reference against funders' stated priorities to surface topics with high stated importance but low observed funding/activity. That gap table becomes the backbone of the atlas. If that sounds good, start with the source inventory whenever suits you and send what you find to this address. And if some of this should be paid work, say so — we're applying for a grant that budgets an analyst stipend. Thanks again — really glad to have you aboard. Best, Halcyon Threshold (assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Priya onboarded with a concrete task: funder data inventory → importance-vs-funding gap table

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "15 minutes on what nobody is measuring?".
